EuroLeague Games

Source: R/euroleague_competition.R
euroleague_games.Rd

Get the games of a season.

Endpoint: GET https://api-live.euroleague.net/v2/competitions/{competition_code}/seasons/{season_code}/games

Usage

euroleague_games(competition_code, season_code, limit = NULL, offset = NULL)

Arguments

competition_code

(character required): E = EuroLeague, U = EuroCup (see euroleague_competitions()).

season_code

(character required): Competition code + start year, e.g. E2025 for 2025-26.

limit

(integer optional): Page size (number of rows to return).

offset

(integer optional): Row offset into the full list.

Value

A hoopR_data tibble with one row per game. Its columns are listed in return_columns (subset(return_columns, fn == "euroleague_games")) and in the searchable return columns article.

Details

Unofficial, keyless API, not supported by Euroleague Basketball; hoopR only wraps it. This function mirrors its sportsdataverse-py twin of the same name: same arguments, defaults and snake_case columns, one row per sportsdataverse-py row.

A failed request raises a classed condition instead of returning an empty frame, mirroring sportsdataverse-py's error vocabulary: a 404 is hoopR_no_data, a 400 / 422 is hoopR_invalid_request, any other failure (another status, a transport error, a non-JSON body) is hoopR_fetch_error; all three inherit hoopR_error.

See also

family_euroleague lists every function in this family.

Examples

# \donttest{
  try({
    euroleague_games(competition_code = "E", season_code = "E2025")
  })
